text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It sharpens fine details in high-motion scenes where current upscalers blur texture, giving a measurable 0.5–1% quality bump without extra compute. The trade-off is a 10–15% speed hit on upscale steps, but the net gain in visual fidelity outweighs the delay for final outputs.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a temporal artifact, not a spatial one. The real risk is wasting 10–15% speed on a tool that doesn’t address the core problem; run a blind A/B test with VFI-Flow’s temporal interpolation instead—if it cuts blur by even 0.5% without breaking the pipeline, that’s the call.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add VFI-Flow to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline. It reconstructs motion blur into sharp frames, directly tackling the core temporal artifact Torque flagged. The trade-off is a 20–25% speed hit on motion-heavy scenes, but the visual gain—even 0.5%—outweighs the cost since blur is the dominant quality killer. Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix blur; VFI-Flow does.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling and VFI-Flow both miss the mark: the first attacks spatial artifacts, the second adds a 20–25% speed hit with no proof it fixes EXCAVA’s blur. Run a blind A/B test against the new **Cerebras-Grit v1.1** temporal model—it claims 0.8% blur reduction at 12% speed cost; if it wins, adopt it, else default to the current pipeline.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a blind A/B test—InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler vs. Cerebras-Grit v1.1 temporal model vs. VFI-Flow’s motion pipeline—on EXCAVA’s worst-case motion blur scenes; the result must prove which delivers ≥0.5% visual gain with the least speed cost, owned by Torque.
